Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Lyra is preparing an internal sign-off package for a small pilot and we need a compact evidence bundle to satisfy our legal and InfoSec teams. Can you provide the following by COB next Tuesday (20 Apr)?

1) A short (1-2 page) summary of cross-border data transfer safeguards you rely on for EU->US processing (legal basis, SCCs/DPF stance, where data is processed).
2) A technical controls summary: encryption at-rest/in-transit, key management (KMS/HSM), access controls, logging/retention windows, and support for customer-managed keys.
3) The current DPA annex draft (if you have a template) and any recommended redlines for controllers in the EU pharma space.
4) Evidence of operational safeguards: audit logs, SOC-2 scope summary, and timeline for producing exportability guidance.
5) A short note on subprocessor list and how you notify customers of changes.

We understand some items may be high-level initially — we just need enough to satisfy Lyra's procurement intake and to share with legal. If you can send a link to a secure drive with documents and point contacts for follow-ups that would be ideal.

Elena

Elena / Marissa — attaching the technical-controls summary as requested. Highlights below.

Attachment: redwood-technical-controls-summary.pdf (summary, 2 pages)

Key points (summary):
- Data flows: Customer data submitted via EU-region endpoints; inference executed on US-hosted clusters (us-west-2) for the pilot. We support region pinning for Dedicated/private deployments.
- Legal transfers: Default mechanism is EU SCCs (controller-to-processor) with contractual DPA annex; Redwood participates in EU adequacy discussions and supports DPF when requested under enterprise contracts.
- Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest. Customer data at rest may be stored with customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key via AWS KMS or HSM integrations) for dedicated/private customers.
- Key management/CMK: Support for customer-managed CMKs for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers can elect to use Redwood-managed KMS, with EKM support in roadmap.
- Logging & retention: Audit logs retained 12 months by default for hosted; configurable retention for Dedicated/Private. Logs include token-level, request/response metadata, and system events — access controlled via RBAC and IAM integrations.
- Subprocessors: Primary cloud infra (AWS), caching CDN provider, logging storage. Full current subprocessor list included in the Drive link. We notify customers 30 days prior to material changes; emergency changes are communicated per contract.

If Lyra needs sample audit log exports or a SOC-2 scope snapshot, we can pull redacted extracts for your review.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Platform Security, Redwood Inference
